with regard to the duty of the Court to fix a just compensation and it has now become settled law that the Court should not succumb to niceties or technicalities, in such matters.
Attempt of the Court should be to equate, as far as possible, the misery on account of the accident with the compensation so th that at the injured/the dependants should not face the vagaries of life on account of the discontinuance of the income earned by the victim.
16. There is another reason why the Court should award proper compensation irrespective of the claim and, if required, even in excess of the claim.
After the amendment of the Act by Act No. 54 of 1994 with effect from 14.11.1994, the Report on motor vehicle accident prepared by the police officer and forwarded to the Claims Tribunal under Sub-section Sub section (6) of Section 158 has to be treated as an Application for Compensation.
In a report on accident, there is no question of any reference to any claim for damages, different heads of damages or such other details.
It is the duty of the Tribunal to build on th that at report and award just, equitable, fair and reasonable compensation with reference to the settled principles on assessment of damages.
Thus, on that ground also we hold that the Tribunal/Court has a duty,
irrespective of the claims made in the Application, if any, to properly award a just, equitable, fair and Application, reasonable compensation, if necessary, ignoring the claim made in the application for compensation."

Thus, keeping in view the aims and object of the beneficial legislation of providing relief to the victims or their families, the total compensation payable to the appellants (petitioners/claimants) is enhanced to Rs.6,24,500/-- (Rupees Six Lakhs twenty four thousand five hundred only).
21. The awarded compensation shall be paid to the claimants within a period of three months from the date of this order order, along with interest at 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of claim petition till the date of payment of compensation to the appellants (petitioner/claimant), with the same terms, which have been mentioned by Ld. Trib Tribunal.
It is further clarified that in case compensation amount due to be paid as on date is not paid within aforementioned stipulated period, same shall be payable to the claimants along with applicable rate of interest @9%p.a.
And, in case any further delay is caused beyond six months from today,
compensation amount payable as on date would be paid to the claimants along with applicable rate of interest @12%p.a from the date of filing claim application till its realization.
22. Distribution of Awarded Compensation:
Therefore, acknowledging her significant role and impact of loss, major part of the compensation i.e. 50% (fifty (fifty-percent) percent) would be paid to her, and remaining 50%of the compensation shall be shared by all the four children, in equal share.
Needless to mention that out of the total payable compensation amount, already paid amount (if any) in compliance to the impugned award would be adjusted.
Therefore, by partly modifying the award, appeal is allowed with the terms indicated here-above.
